title: Launch plan + channel calendar for Latency/$ benchmark report
creator: Talia Benson
project: Latency per Dollar Benchmark Report (Production Economics)
description:
Objective
Create and execute the integrated launch plan for the public-facing “Latency per Dollar” benchmark report across channels (landing page, blog/docs, email/lifecycle, social, partners, analysts/press, and sales enablement). This ticket is the source of truth for sequencing, owners, and readiness criteria.

Why this matters
We’re positioning Redwood Inference as the credible reference for production economics (latency/$) across open models and regions. The launch must be coordinated to (1) land a consistent narrative, (2) avoid over-claiming, (3) route inbound to the right motions (Hosted API self-serve vs Dedicated/Private sales-assisted), and (4) protect credibility (methodology clarity + variance language).

Launch date / timing
- Target public launch date (TBD → locked): 2025-02-25 (Tue)
- Press/analyst embargo: 2025-02-25 06:00 PT (confirm with Camila)
- Internal enablement deadline: 2025-02-21 EOD
- Web content freeze: 2025-02-24 12:00 PT (only critical fixes after)

Primary deliverables (public)
1) Benchmark report landing page + downloadable PDF
2) Blog post announcing the report (with key charts, strong methodology callouts, and CTAs)
3) Methodology appendix page + FAQ entries (variance, caching, region routing, how to interpret)
4) Email sequence (announcement + 2 follow-ups)
5) Social pack (LinkedIn/X) + UTM plan
6) Partner co-marketing kit distribution + co-branded posts where applicable

Internal deliverables
1) Field enablement package: field deck + one-pager + objection handling + approved claims
2) Support readiness: macros + escalation path
3) Post-launch metrics dashboard plan (traffic → download → signup/meeting → pipeline influence)

Readiness gates (go/no-go)
1) Methodology sign-off complete (Jonas + Claire)
2) Claims guidelines applied across all copy (Michael Grant approval for external-facing artifacts)
3) Public tables/PDF artifacts served reliably (ENG-2872 + platform caching plan validated)
4) UTM + attribution tested end-to-end (landing → download → signup/meeting; Tyler)
5) Sales enablement materials posted and training completed (Jordan/Markus)
6) Support macros published + escalation on-call schedule confirmed (Dev/Jasmine)
7) Capacity/SLO guardrails in place for benchmark reproduction inquiries (Neha/Sean)

KPIs (launch week)
- Landing page unique visitors
- Report downloads (unique + total)
- New Hosted API signups attributed (first-touch + last-touch)
- “Book a consult” meetings booked + show rate
- Pipeline influenced (30-day view) for Dedicated/Private
- Support volume tagged “benchmark report” + median first response time

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: Over-interpretation of results (“Redwood is always fastest/cheapest”).
  - Mitigation: consistent language on workloads/variance, confidence bands, region differences, and no absolute superiority claims.
- Risk: Prospects see different latency in their app.
  - Mitigation: publish reproduction guide + FAQ explaining routing, concurrency, prompt shape, caching/batching differences.
- Risk: Launch traffic or tables serving reliability issues.
  - Mitigation: pre-warm caches, CDN caching, rollback plan for downloads, war-room monitoring.

Open questions (resolved)
- Primary angle: latency/$ as the headline; cost-only relegated to supporting context. (Resolved 2025-02-12)
- APAC region inclusion in headlines: include in tables; avoid over-indexing in hero copy to reduce debate on workload locality. (Resolved 2025-02-14)
